newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks hit new record on economic plan hype.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks hit new record on economic plan hype.

text.p: Mexican stocks surged to record highs for the second day in a row on Wednesday as foreign investors gave a thumbs up to President Ernesto Zedillo's three-year economic plan calling for higher economic growth.
The leading IPC index of 37 shares smashed the 4,100-point barrier, climbing 61.50 points, or 1.51 percent, to 4,121.56 points. Tuesday's record close was 4,060.06 points.
Wednesday's record close was the 23rd so far this year.
"There was buying pretty much across the board, with a lot of foreign interest. It was a combination of a lot of things, especially the new economic plan," a dealer said.
Investors shrugged off a rise in interest rates late on Tuesday and bid up prices in heavy trade of 183.5 million shares, led mostly by market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico.
Market heavyweight Telmex L shares rose 3.45 percent and accounted for 18 percent of all shares traded.
Telmex was firm following news it would be compensated by competitors for its costs in outfitting its network for competition.
The market did not react to a nearly one percentage point rise in the bellwether 28-day Cetes on Tuesday, which rose on jitters ahead of next month's national elections.
But some dealers said the stock market was looking forward and did not see further increases in rates.
There were 110 active shares, with gainers besting losers 46-42.
Retailer Autrey shares rose 11.59 percent on news it would buy the country's fourth largest chain of drugstores, Drogueros SA.

Paper company Kimberly-Clark de Mexico, a subsidiary of Kimberly-Clark, surged 5.82 percent in its A series shares after Mexico's Federal Competition Commission gave final approval for its merger with Compania Industrial de San Cristobal SA.
